Wikipedia: the background is completely gilt
Wikipedia: the painting uses the difficult to obtain lapis lazuli

highlight.text: The artists' use of expensive lacquer, extensive gold leafing and the difficult to obtain lapis lazuli in the painting demonstrates the communal prestige of the commission.

source.label: Wikipedia: Simone Martini, a Sienese precursor of the style
Wikipedia: Simone Martini, Duccio's pupil, is among the Sienese school's most important artists

work.text: Considered Martini's masterwork and one of the most outstanding works of Gothic painting, the work was originally painted for a side altar in Siena Cathedral.

source.author: Wikipedia contributors
source.title: Annunciation with Saint Margaret and Saint Ansanus

work.text: Lippo Memmi painted the two saints who stand one on either side of the central scene. But the Annunciation itself is entirely the work of Simone.
As you look at the angel's mantle it is as if you were seeing the young sunlight on driven snow.

source.author: Bernard Berenson
source.title: The Central Italian Painters of the Renaissance

moment.text: The work, in both size and style, has no similarities with any other contemporary painting in Italy. It can be compared instead to French illuminated manuscripts of that time, as well as to paintings from Germany or England.

source.author: Wikipedia contributors
source.title: Annunciation with Saint Margaret and Saint Ansanus

moment.text: This is a picture the affected tenderness of which might well have had influence on the school of mystic painters.

source.author: J. A. Crowe and G. B. Cavalcaselle
source.title: A History of Painting in Italy, vol. 3: The Sienese School of the Fourteenth Century (ed. Langton Douglas)

matters.text: Mary, sitting on a throne, is portrayed at the moment that she is startled out of her reading, reacting with a graceful and composed reluctance, looking with surprise at the celestial messenger.

source.author: Wikipedia contributors
source.title: Annunciation with Saint Margaret and Saint Ansanus

matters.text: The Virgin in the act of receiving the angel, but shrinking with a sidelong action and with affected softness of motion from him, is rendered with an extraordinary exaggeration of tenderness in the closed lids and hardly apparent iris of the eyes.

source.author: J. A. Crowe and G. B. Cavalcaselle
source.title: A History of Painting in Italy, vol. 3: The Sienese School of the Fourteenth Century (ed. Langton Douglas)

matters.text: along the path of the dove, viewers see Gabriel's utterance: ave gratia plena dominvs tecvm ('Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee.').
